resources.string: When another app opens a Play Store link with a normal VIEW intent (market:// or play.google.com), Android can send that link here. We convert it to HTTPS and open your browser — same path as the Test button, but only if the system routes the link to us.

This is not a permission problem we can flip on. (1) Play deep links only reach us if we are the chosen handler. (2) Apps that hardcode the Play Store package never call us. (3) In-app Google Sign-In uses Play services APIs — install GrapheneOS sandboxed Google Play for that; this app cannot see or replace that flow.
Checking which apps handle Play links…
Open “Open by default” for this app
Uses a normal market:// VIEW intent so Android picks the handler (like other apps). If Play Store or a browser is Always, we will not run.
Setup so other apps use us

1. Tap “Test as external link”. If a chooser appears, pick Play Redirect → Always.
2. Or open “Open by default” and allow supported links / clear other apps’ defaults for Play.
3. If Play Store (com.android.vending) is installed, clear its defaults or it will keep market://.
4. Debug ON → open a Play link from another app → Save log. You should see RedirectActivity lines if we were chosen.
Logs intents delivered to Play Redirect only. Empty log after using another app = that app did not send us the link (different handler or explicit Play Store intent).
